suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-21 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited endoscopy cohort of patients over age 50 with documented iron-deficiency anemia identified peptic ulcer disease among the upper gastrointestinal findings. Require documented peptic-ulcer disease with bleeding or other clinically relevant iron loss and separately established iron-deficiency anemia with compatible chronology; the cohort identifies an upper gastrointestinal source in selected patients but does not establish that any individual's anemia was caused by peptic-ulcer disease. Preserve gastrointestinal malignancy, other gastrointestinal bleeding, malabsorption, dietary deficiency, chronic inflammatory disease, renal disease, hemolysis, medications, and other causes of anemia. Do not infer anemia from a peptic-ulcer diagnosis without objective hematologic evidence or compatible bleeding history. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of peptic-ulcer-disease and anemia
Objective iron studies and hemoglobin records establishing iron-deficiency anemia
Endoscopy or other records documenting ulcer location, activity, and bleeding or iron-loss phenotype
Chronology compatible with the approved bounded proposition

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented peptic-ulcer disease with bleeding or other clinically relevant iron loss and separately established iron-deficiency anemia with compatible chronology; preserve competing causes.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited endoscopy cohort reports peptic-ulcer disease among upper gastrointestinal findings in selected patients with iron-deficiency anemia, supporting a bounded clinical association for research rather than an individual causal conclusion.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; the guard explicitly limits the claim to an association requiring individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A bleeding or chronically oozing peptic ulcer could provide gastrointestinal iron loss and thereby be temporally associated with iron-deficiency anemia, but this mechanism is only a research hypothesis for an individual until bleeding and hematologic chronology are documented.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The selected endoscopy cohort does not establish that peptic-ulcer disease caused any individual's anemia, and competing sources of blood loss or impaired erythropoiesis must be evaluated before any nexus opinion.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent diagnoses, objective iron studies, ulcer bleeding phenotype, and compatible chronology remain necessary; the selected cohort does not resolve individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: gastrointestinal malignancy or other gastrointestinal bleeding
